clue.text: First letters, out of order, are included in bold

indicators.note: the word 'are' is included, placed inside the jumbled alphabet letters
letters out of order are jumbled into a new sequence

parts.note: the first letters of the alphabet, A to F
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's note that some initials have been scrambled and printed in heavy type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First letters' looks like the initials of words in the clue, but means the opening letters of the alphabet; 'out of order' scrambles them and 'included' takes ARE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold in the sense of shameless or brazen, without any attempt at concealment.

clue.text: For composer, what inspires rhapsody?

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ..., the English composer and Master of the Queen's Music
intense joy is what makes someone go into rhapsodies

explanation.surface: A question about where a composer finds the inspiration for a rhapsody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhapsody' tempts the solver towards the musical form, but here it means ecstatic expression of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was a twentieth-century English composer, and perfect happiness is what sets people rhapsodising.

clue.text: Surviving European chief in scene of fighting

indicators.note: the European and chief go in, placed inside the scene of fighting

parts.note: a boxing ring is where bouts are fought
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A European leader who has come through a battlefield alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what is still left or still existing after others have gone.

clue.text: Supporting English gallery holding second preview

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: the gallery holds the second, with it placed inside

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery backing English art keeps a second room for a sneak preview.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or glimpse of something still to come, much like a preview.

clue.text: Problem seeing how to solve rubik's cube, but not crossword

definitions.text: Problem seeing how to solve rubik's cube, but not crossword

parts.words: Problem seeing how to solve rubik's cube, but not crossword
parts.note: a Rubik's cube is solved by matching coloured faces, while a crossword grid is only black and white, so an eye condition affecting hues would hinder the first but not the second

explanation.surface: Someone can't work out the cube puzzle, though they manage crosswords fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem seeing how to solve' reads as being stumped by the puzzle, but 'seeing' is literal: a sight defect.
explanation.definitionFit: An inability to tell certain hues apart would make matching the faces of the cube impossible while leaving a monochrome grid untouched.

clue.text: Artistic skill seen in piece moved on board vessel

parts.note: a draughtsman is a playing piece in draughts, the British name for checkers
a ship is a sea-going vessel

explanation.surface: Artistry is apparent in the way a piece is moved aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but it is the draughts board; DRAUGHTS is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in technical drawing or sketching is an artistic talent.

clue.text: Test beginner with foolish rubbish

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter, taken from test

parts.note: rash means reckless or foolish

explanation.surface: A novice who takes a test recklessly produces worthless work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean worthless stuff or nonsense, fit to be thrown away.

clue.text: High point for Ireland, securing one triple crown

indicators.note: the Irish high point secures one, holding it inside

parts.note: the Hill of Tara was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ireland's peak moment comes in winning a rugby Triple Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rugby's Triple Crown, which Ireland competes for; the definition is the Pope's three-tiered crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal headdress has three tiers of crowns, so a triple crown describes it exactly.

clue.text: Leading article on crisis

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a head is a critical point, as in 'come to a head'

explanation.surface: A leading newspaper article about a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front or in the lead in a race or contest.

clue.text: Historical pioneer rode south willy-nilly

indicators.note: willy-nilly means in a haphazard way, so the letters of rode and south are mixed up

explanation.surface: An early explorer rode southward without any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willy-nilly' scrambles RODE and SOUTH together. The answer is the Greek writer known as the father of history.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century BC Greek writer is called the father of history, the first to research past events systematically.

clue.text: Two marks in one exam — that's bad

indicators.note: the two marks go in, inside one exam

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an oral is a spoken examination
M is the abbreviation for the German mark, so two give two M's

explanation.surface: Getting two marks in a single exam is a poor result.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or morally wrong behaviour is bad in the ethical sense.

clue.text: A colleague said you are incompetent

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague

indicators.note: said means the words you are are spoken, sounding like two letters

parts.note: the words you are, spoken quickly, sound like the letters U R as in text-speak

explanation.surface: A fellow worker tells you that you are hopeless at your job.
explanation.definitionFit: An unskilled or inexpert person, as opposed to a professional, does a job badly.

clue.text: Garment workers

definitions.meaning: a simple loose dress or undergarment
a group of employees working the same period, as on the night team

explanation.surface: People who make clothes in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose straight dress is one sense, and a team on duty for a set period is the other.

clue.text: Imprudent, like man liable to be taken on board

definitions.text: like man liable to be taken on board
definitions.meaning: a chessman left unprotected on the board can be captured

explanation.surface: Someone foolish enough to get dragged aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken on board' suggests a ship, but a man is a chess piece and taken means captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless speech is incautious, and a piece with no defender can be captured.

clue.text: Master carpenter

definitions.meaning: Mr ..., the schoolmaster in the novel Goodbye, Mr ...
a traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter

explanation.surface: A highly skilled woodworker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master carpenter' reads as one skilled tradesman, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional teacher of Goodbye, Mr Chips was a schoolmaster, and a woodworker is nicknamed for the shavings he makes.

clue.text: Emerged from east, between two rivers

indicators.note: east goes between the two rivers, placed inside their pairing

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge and the Forth through Scotland
the Cam flows through Cambridge and the Forth through Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone surfaced from the east, in the land between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean came out or appeared, the phrase being an old-fashioned way of saying it.

clue.text: Away from shore on vessel, lose one's nerve

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a bottle is a vessel for liquid
boats away from shore are out at sea

explanation.surface: Far out at sea on a ship, a sailor panics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface vessel is a boat, but the wordplay vessel is a container; BOTTLE also means courage in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for flinching from something through fear, since bottle means courage.

clue.text: Partnership not involving union organization

parts.note: a marriage made for affection rather than one arranged by families; 'union organization' looks like a trade body but means arranging the wedding

explanation.surface: A business alliance formed without any trade union involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union organization' suggests a trade union, but the union is a marriage and organization means arranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage entered for affection rather than one arranged by others for property or alliance.

clue.text: Oddly we tear our clothes, visibly worn

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of we tear our are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, we rip our clothes so that the damage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges WE TEAR OUR; it does not mean taking odd letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn on top, such as coats, are the ones seen by others.

clue.text: Element changed in two thousand guineas

indicators.note: the changed letters sit in between the two thousands

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two give two M's
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two give two M's

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of guineas are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some element converted into two thousand guineas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of guineas, and 'in' sets the result between the two M's. The surface plays on the 2000 Guineas, a classic English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A light silvery metal, number twelve in the periodic table, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Nose and eyes, from what we hear, often indicated by hands

definitions.text: Nose and eyes, from what we hear
definitions.meaning: spoken, these words sound like noes and ayes, the calls in a parliamentary division
a show of hands is a common way to decide by ballot

explanation.surface: Facial features described by ear, and frequently pointed to with hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose and eyes' said aloud gives 'noes and ayes', the answers in a parliamentary ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes and ayes are the two kinds of ballot cast in Parliament, and a show of hands is another way of counting them.

clue.text: It's illegal, getting drunk in Bedford

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated, so the letters of in Bedford are reeling about

explanation.surface: Being drunk in the town of Bedford is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedford is an English county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by law is not allowed, just as an illegal act is.

clue.text: Be impervious to dance around piano

indicators.note: the dance goes around piano, holding it inside

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by a dance performed around a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or resist something, as a coating keeps out water.

clue.text: To sleep in the middle of it is inappropriate

indicators.note: the sleep is placed in the middle of it

parts.note: taken as written
to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: Dozing off in the middle of something is not the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or ill-fitting for the occasion, much as an unfitting remark is.

clue.text: What's earned, taken back in retirement

indicators.note: taken back means the letters are read in reverse order
in means the letters lie inside the word retirement

explanation.surface: Something deserved is lost on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks TIREM out of retirement and 'taken back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth or excellence that deserves reward, as in pay by results.

clue.text: Stopping revolt at last, become elevated as emperor

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, with the letter put inside
in a down clue, elevated means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to become someone is to suit them, as a hat might

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of revolt

explanation.surface: Ending a rebellion, a ruler rises in status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns SUIT upwards into TIUS, and 'Stopping' puts T, the last of 'revolt', inside it. 'become' is the verb meaning to look good on.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor of the first century AD, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Succeed with combination of fabrics

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Win through by mixing different cloths.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow and take over from someone, as a successor does.

clue.text: Difficult situation prophetic work covers time and time again

indicators.note: the prophetic work covers time, holding it inside

parts.note: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament prophets
a second T, another abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tricky spot covered repeatedly in a book of prophecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put on the spot under pressure, as on a quiz show's grilling chair.

clue.text: Crowd welcoming half-century for top English scorer

indicators.note: the crowd welcomes half-century, taking it inside

parts.note: a host is a large crowd or multitude
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fans cheer an English batsman reaching fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a half-century is fifty runs) misleads: the scorer writes music scores, Gustav Holst of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was a leading English composer, and composers write scores.

clue.text: Is, perhaps, in error, producing precious stones

indicators.note: in error means wrongly, so the letters of is perhaps are set out wrongly

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone is wrong about which jewels are produced.
explanation.definitionFit: These blue gems are a kind of corundum and rank among the precious jewels.
